title: Meet John Doe

evidence.note: A 1941 film needed a 28th-year renewal around 1968-1969. I read the 1968 and 1969 Catalog of Copyright Entries motion-picture volumes by automated text fetch, but only about 20% of each file was readable. The renewal sections were not reached, so I found no renewal entry but cannot call that a negative search. A hand search of the renewal sections, plus the Copyright Office records, is still needed.

evidence.note: Wikipedia says the Library of Congress made a preservation negative in the 1970s, and that a 2001 digital restoration by Ken Barnes' Laureate Presentations used the best available European print and was released on DVD by Sanctuary and VCI. I did not check these against a primary page. Anything a restoration adds, such as new titles, a new score or other added material, can carry its own copyright. A faithful transfer adds none.

editorial:
Meet John Doe is a 1941 Frank Capra film starring Gary Cooper and Barbara Stanwyck. The Internet Archive lists Frank Capra Productions, Inc. as the creator of one copy. Creators look for it because copies are easy to find online.

The rights trap is that the print's status is not settled here. A film from 1941 is free only if its 28th-year renewal was never filed. I could not read the renewal sections of the 1968 and 1969 Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes in full, so no non-renewal is confirmed. Score, source story and any restored copy each need separate checks.
faq: Is Meet John Doe in the public domain?

Not confirmed. A 1941 film is free only if no renewal was filed in its 28th year. My check of the 1968 and 1969 Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes was incomplete, so the print stays undetermined. Search the renewal sections and the Copyright Office records yourself before relying on it.
Can I use any copy I find online?

Not automatically. Even if the print is free, a copy can add protected material such as new titles, a new score or other additions. Use a copy whose source you can check, and do not rip a copy-protected disc, because that can violate 17 U.S.C. 1201.
